title: Some moons are bigger than planets

narration.heading: Moon vs planet
narration.text: You think moons are small? Some of them are bigger than a planet.

narration.heading: Europa
narration.text: Meet Europa, an icy moon of Jupiter. Under its ice may be two or three times the water in Earth's oceans.

narration.heading: Our Moon
narration.text: Our own Moon is a little bigger, about three and a half thousand kilometres across.

narration.heading: Mercury
narration.text: Now a real planet. Mercury, the closest one to the Sun, is almost five thousand kilometres wide.

narration.heading: Titan
narration.text: But Saturn's moon Titan is wider still. It even has thicker air than Earth, and lakes of liquid methane.

narration.heading: Moon beats planet
narration.text: Titan is about six percent wider than Mercury. A moon, beating a planet.

narration.heading: Ganymede
narration.text: And the biggest moon of all? Jupiter's Ganymede, wider than Mercury, with a hidden ocean under its ice.

narration.heading: The twist
narration.text: The twist? Mercury is smaller, but heavier. Ganymede has less than half of Mercury's mass.

narration.heading: Why?
narration.text: Mercury's metal core fills most of its width. Ganymede is half rock, half ice. So which is bigger: wider, or heavier?

hook.banner: Can a moon beat a planet?

skit.text: Wider or heavier? I just say my files are compressed.

titles: What if moons were lined up next to a planet?
Some moons are bigger than planets
youtube.description: Europa, our Moon, Mercury, Titan and Ganymede side by side at true scale, and why the planet Mercury still outweighs the two moons that are wider than it.

sources.claim: Europa's mean radius is 1,560.8 km, slightly smaller than Earth's Moon; its subsurface ocean holds two to three times the volume of Earth's oceans
The Moon's mean radius is 1,737.4 km (about 3,475 km across)
Mercury is the planet nearest the Sun, radius about 2,440 km, with a metallic core of about 2,074 km radius, about 85% of the planet's radius
Mercury's mean radius is 2,439.4 km (diameter 4,878.8 km) and its mass 3.3011 × 10²³ kg; it is smaller but more massive than Ganymede and Titan
Titan's mean radius is about 2,575 km (5,150 km across), about 6% wider than Mercury; surface pressure about 1.45 atm, denser than Earth's; lakes of liquid methane
Ganymede, the largest moon, has a mean radius of 2,632.27 km and a mass of 1.48 × 10²³ kg, 45% of Mercury's; it has an internal ocean and is made of rock and water in roughly equal proportions
